Deal_Title: Seminole Tribe of Florida places $459 million of special obligation bonds ($240 million Series 2007A tax-exempt due 2027 and $219 million Series 2007B taxable due 2020)
Counterparty_or_Funder: Private placement investors (Rule 144A / private tribal bond market)
Event_Type: Special obligation bond issuance rated at pricing
Status: Rated; proposed at the date of the rating action
Value_Type: Aggregate principal of the two proposed special obligation bond series rated by Moody's on this date ($240,000,000 Series 2007A tax-exempt due 2027 + $219,000,000 Series 2007B taxable due 2020)
Description: On September 14, 2007 Moody's Investors Service raised the Seminole Tribe of Florida's existing Series A and B gaming division bonds and term loan to Baa3 and assigned a Ba1 rating to the Tribe's proposed $240 million Series 2007A tax-exempt special obligation bonds due 2027 and $219 million Series 2007B taxable special obligation bonds due 2020. These are Rule 144A-style private tribal placements that never appear on SEC EDGAR. A later Moody's action (April 2, 2013) confirms the series were issued and itemises them as $113 million 5.250% due 2027, $60 million 5.750% due 2022, $66 million 5.50% due 2024 (2007A tranches) and $219 million 7.804% due 2020 (2007B).
Native_Connection: The Seminole Tribe of Florida is a federally recognized tribe and the issuer of the bonds in its own governmental capacity. Ownership verified: Yes.
Source_1_Type: Moody's Investors Service rating action (public press release, retrieved via Internet Archive)
Source_2_Type: Moody's rating action of 2013-04-02 itemising the issued 2007A/2007B series (corroboration)
Notes: Rule 144A / private tribal debt: this transaction is absent from SEC EDGAR by construction. Do NOT sum with ND-2013-301: the 2013 term loan B refinances a different instrument (the 2007 term loan due 2014), not these bonds.

Description: Moody's raised Choctaw Resort Development Enterprise's Corporate Family Rating to Caa1 from Caa3 on March 14, 2012 'after the Enterprise completed a refinancing of its bank debt that extended its debt maturities and improved its liquidity profile.' The retrieved release states that Choctaw Resort 'recently entered into a new $78 million senior secured term loan agreement due February 2017 (unrated by Moody's) with various lenders' and that 'the proceeds from the new loan were mainly used to fully repay the Enterprise's pre-existing bank term loan that was scheduled to mature in May 2012.' Moody's withdrew the rating on the pre-existing term loan.
Native_Connection: Choctaw Resort Development Enterprise is an unincorporated economic development enterprise of the Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians, a federally recognized tribe. Ownership verified: Yes.
Source_1_Type: Moody's Investors Service rating action (public press release, retrieved via Internet Archive)

Instrument chain: superseded by the $145 million term loan in ND-2014-301 (the $70 million balance refinanced there is this same loan) - never sum ND-2012-301 and ND-2014-301.

Description: On April 2, 2013 Moody's upgraded the Seminole Tribe of Florida's ratings to Baa3 and 'assigned a Baa3 to the Tribe's proposed $750 million term B due 2020.' The retrieved release states that 'proceeds from the proposed term loan, along with balance sheet cash, will be used to refinance the Tribe's existing term loan due 2014 of which $794 million is currently outstanding,' and that the rating on the existing term loan 'will be withdrawn upon the closing of the new facilities.' The upgrade moved the Tribe to low investment grade and Moody's withdrew its Corporate Family Rating because the Tribe was no longer considered a high-yield issuer.

Deal_Title: Downstream Development Authority (Quapaw Nation) closes $270 million senior secured notes due 2023 and a $40 million term loan

Native_Party_Type: Tribal authority / instrumentality of a federally recognized tribe
Counterparty_or_Funder: Rule 144A note investors and term loan lenders (unnamed in the retrieved document)
Event_Type: Senior secured note issuance and term loan closing
Value_Type: Aggregate principal of the two new instruments ($270,000,000 senior secured notes due 2023 + $40,000,000 term loan)
Description: Moody's upgraded Downstream Development Authority's Corporate Family Rating to B2 from B3 on February 22, 2018. The retrieved release states 'this rating action follows the closing of DDA's new $40 million term loan (unrated) and new $270 million senior secured notes due 2023,' and that 'proceeds from these new debt issues were used to refinance DDA's $32 million first lien credit facility and $265 million senior secured notes due 2019.' $42 million of the old notes had not been tendered and DDA planned to redeem the remainder on March 3, 2018. Moody's covenant quality assessment of January 26, 2018 had scored the deal as $265 million of senior secured notes due 2023, so the notes were upsized to $270 million between launch and closing.
Native_Connection: Downstream Development Authority is a wholly owned unincorporated instrumentality of the Quapaw Nation (Quapaw Tribe of Oklahoma), a federally recognized tribe, and owns Downstream Casino Resort. Ownership verified: Yes.

Deal_Title: Mohegan Tribal Gaming Authority closes $1.175 billion second lien note refinancing
Native_Party: Mohegan Tribal Gaming Authority (Mohegan Tribe of Indians of Connecticut)
Native_Party_Type: Tribal gaming authority / instrumentality of a federally recognized tribe
Counterparty_or_Funder: Second lien note investors and first lien revolving lenders (unnamed in the retrieved document)

Value_Type: Principal of the second lien notes due 2026 issued in the refinancing
Description: On January 13, 2021 Moody's assigned a Caa1 rating to Mohegan Tribal Gaming Authority's proposed $1.175 billion second lien notes due 2026 and a B1 rating to a proposed amended and extended $263 million first lien revolver. Proceeds, together with $49 million of cash, were to refinance MTGA's $232 million term loan A and $814 million term loan B in full at par plus $55 million of other debt, and to repay $100 million of the $197 million then drawn under the existing $250 million revolver. The follow-on rating action of January 29, 2021 states that 'on January 26, MTGA closed on a refinancing that had a meaningful positive impact on the company's liquidity,' giving a day-level closing date, and that the revolver expiry was extended 18 months to April 2023.
Native_Connection: The Mohegan Tribal Gaming Authority is an instrumentality of the Mohegan Tribe of Indians of Connecticut, a federally recognized tribe. Ownership verified: Yes.

USE-OF-PROCEEDS TRAP AVOIDED: the $232 million term loan A, $814 million term loan B, $55 million of other debt and $100 million revolver repayment are all repayments and are NOT added.
